<!--
  product-module — a deliverable (an application or a library), an area of one, or a page describing
    shared content: a named grouping of related features.
  Lives at: `product/modules/<module>.md`.
  Authorship: canonical. SLO: 180d.
  Owner: fixed to `product`, do not substitute.
  Discipline: a module is NOT a feature — it groups them; a member of a set a feature works over
    is not a feature either (the product README's feature boundary); list each feature as its own
    [[features/<module>/<feature-slug>]] page, do not inline feature flows here. A module is a
    deliverable at the top of `product/modules/` or an area nested under one, at most two levels of
    areas deep: an area's page sits at `product/modules/<deliverable>/<area>.md`, beside the directory
    holding its own areas, and links its parent in `related:`; each module's own page sits beside its
    directory, at `product/modules/<module>.md` (`storefront/catalog/search` is
    `modules/storefront/catalog/search.md`) — never `overview.md` or `index.md`. A `_shared/`
    directory holds shared content rather than a module — at the top of `product/modules/` for content
    no deliverable owns, under a deliverable for content only its areas share — and needs no page; one
    that describes it sits at `modules/_shared.md` or `modules/<deliverable>/_shared.md`. A
    deliverable's areas get no section of their own: the product index lists them beneath it.
  Columns: Open questions — Question | Owner | Resume condition.
  Extra frontmatter: `kind` (application | library | area | shared) is REQUIRED, and where the page
    sits decides which value is legal — [[_authoring:wiki-page-placement#where-a-page-may-sit]]
    states the rule. `application` — a product its users adopt and run on its own, even where one of
    its features needs a feature of another application. `library` — composed into this wiki's
    applications, never adopted alone; a building-block SDK is one, while a client SDK for one of
    this wiki's applications is part of that application. `area` — a functional area of exactly one
    deliverable. `shared` — a page at or beneath a `_shared/` directory, describing shared content
    rather than a deliverable or an area.
    Who the module is for is `audience`, not `kind`. `audience` (customer | internal) is REQUIRED —
    always set it; determines whether the module is product-facing (customer) or internal/ops
    (internal). `platforms` (any subset of web | mobile | api | email | notification | export) is
    OPTIONAL — to omit it, delete its whole frontmatter line. Do not leave {{KIND}}, {{AUDIENCE}} or
    {{PLATFORMS}} unsubstituted, and do not leave `platforms: []` empty — all fail the `/wiki-lint`
    vocab check on the authored page. `depends-on` is OPTIONAL — dash-list of `[[modules/<module>]]` /
    `[[features/<module>/<feature-slug>]]` / `[[app-base]]` links naming hard build-order
    prerequisites. Distinct from `related:` (general cross-references). `/wiki-lint` enforces it:
    every entry takes the `[[…]]` form, resolving within this sub-wiki unless it carries a domain
    prefix; the page it names must be a `product-module`, a `feature`, or `app-base`; the graph the
    entries form must be acyclic; and each edge follows the composition direction
    [[_authoring:wiki-page-placement#what-a-page-may-depend-on]] states. Unlike `platforms`, an empty
    `depends-on: []` is fine — leave it when none.
  Disposition: keep every header; "None." when empty.
  Substitute: {{TITLE}} {{DATE}} {{CONFIDENCE}} {{ORIGINATION}} {{AUDIENCE}} {{KIND}} {{PLATFORMS}}.
-->

## Navigation
<!-- One short paragraph: the module's entry point(s) into the app, the list→detail→form routing
     pattern across its surfaces, and — for a multi-surface module — which surfaces live where.
     Keep it to a few sentences; the per-surface detail lives in each feature's ## Surfaces.
     This side owns the module's entry points and its in-module routing; the cross-module sitemap
     and the URL scheme belong to the design `information-architecture`, which names this module.
     A module-level surface no single feature owns — a dashboard, a landing view — is its own
     hub-shaped feature: name it here and detail it there, rather than specifying it on this page.
     A module page is a table of contents, and a surface specified here is one no feature's
     acceptance criteria reach. -->

## Quality attributes

<!-- How well this module must work as a whole — speed, availability, security, accessibility. One

     own. -->

## Boundaries
